title: Safety Drop-in: micro-talk + ops Q&A (internal prep)
body:
Purpose: quick (2-3 min) drop-in at next all-hands and follow-up Q&A for M+E about weekend-mode decisions and what to expect. This is a personal prep/scratchpad — keep it informal.

Key framing (30s):
- Why: we want teams to be confident — tell them minimal disruption plan, where to look if they need help.
- Tone: calm, pragmatic, operational empathy. acknowledge friction but show clear owner and fallback.
- Ask: 1-sentence ask to engineers: check critical alerts, verify runs for high-priority jobs before 17:00 PT Fri.

2-min micro-talk bullets (tight):
- Heads-up: weekend-mode scheduled Sat 23:00 -> Sun 06:00 PT; primary reason: infra maintenance + capacity reshuffle.
- Expected impact: no public API downtime expected; possible brief throttling on embeddings during peak length windows; we will route heavier retries to dedicated pool.
- For customers: auto-fallbacks active (hosted->dedicated routing); we will not change billing model.
- If you are oncall: watch slack channel #oncall (linked). Follow runbook step 1-4 if alerts > P1.
- Contact: ops lead Tomas Vega; escalation: eng-sre pager (primary), platform-eng (secondary).

Micro Q&A (prep answers):
Q: Will this affect SLAs?
A: No SLA change planned; we have capacity guardrails and can spin dedicated capacity if we observe degradation beyond thresholds in first hour. If degraded we'll open an incident and update status.redwood.ai.

Q: Why short window / why now?
A: Coordinated kernel upgrades + a hotfix for batching regressions. Risk reduces if we do small window with controlled rollback.

Q: What should product teams communicate to customers?
A: One-line to put in release notes: "Planned infra maintenance Saturday, low-risk to API performance; automatic fallbacks in place. Contact support for concerns." Keep it simple.

Q: What if an endpoint is slow?
A: First: confirm via tracing (console -> route dashboard). If tail latency > 300ms for >5% tokens across 5m, trigger the autoscale play and open a P1.

Open items / TODOs before talk:
- Finalize single-slide visual of routing fallback flow (who takes traffic when). Assigned: Aisha. Due: 2025-11-04 EOD.
- Short link to runbook in slides. Done: link placeholder in linked_artifacts.
- Quick confirm from product that no customer comms scheduled overlapping. Ping: Mikaela.
- Rehearse 30s taglines with CEO (maybe keep CEO line 1 optional).

Handy script (30s cadence):
- "Quick ops update: we have planned maintenance this weekend. Low risk to customers — our automatic fallbacks and dedicated routing will protect most traffic. If you see anything concerning, go to #oncall and follow the runbook; ops will monitor live. Thanks."

Notes-to-self:
- Keep wording non-alarmist. Avoid deep technicals in all-hands; invite SRE office hours after for detailed walk-through.
- Bring 1 visual: control flow (hosted -> fallback) + one metric (current error rate baseline).
- Add two short sample Slack replies for support team to paste.

Sample Slack reply (support canned):
- "Thanks for the report — this is likely related to planned maintenance this weekend. We're monitoring; can you share request id? If it's urgent, escalate in #oncall and we'll route to SRE."

Fallback checklist (ops):
- Confirm autoscale policy active (check console).
- Verify KV cache stability on dedicated pool.
- Ensure rollback image staged and tested in canary.
- Pager rotation: confirm primary is online and has routing privileges.

Post-talk follow-ups:
- 1:30pm Mon: ops office hours (15-20m) deep-dive for product and platform owners.
- Publish quick recap to #engineering and attach runbook + links.

Open questions to resolve with Tomas:
- Do we want a customer-facing status update (email) or only support FAQ? (privilege: product decision).
- Are we comfortable with the embeddings throttle for short windows or should we pre-warm dedicated instances? Cost vs risk tradeoff.

Rough timings:
- Fri 12:00: finalize slide + canned messages.
- Fri 15:00: sync with product (Mikaela).
- Fri 16:00: final rehearsal.

Random scratch ideas (maybe useful):
- Tiny A/B: enable short burst capacity for heavy embedding jobs only; monitor cost metric delta.
- Add brief 'what to expect after' bullet: we'll publish a short postmortem if anything notable occurs.

End of scratchpad.

-- Rae
